title: Affine criterion for schematic density of finitely many principal opens
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in A$, with $n\geq0$. Write $A_{f_i}=A[1/f_i]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and $D(f_i)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A:f_i\notin\mathfrak p\}$. Put $U=\bigcup_i D(f_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$. The natural map $A\to\bigoplus_i A_{f_i}$ is injective if and only if $A\to A^{\oplus n}$, $a\mapsto(f_1a,\ldots,f_na)$, is injective. For the open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-open-immersion], these conditions are also equivalent to injectivity of the natural restriction map of sheaves $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\to j_*\mathcal O_U$.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 0565 (lemma-when-injective-covering), applied to M=A; Morphisms, Tag 056C (example-scheme-theoretic-closure) and Tag 01RE (lemma-characterize-scheme-theoretically-dense)

proof.text: Write $\lambda:A\to\bigoplus_i A_{f_i}$ for the localization map and $\mu:A\to A^{\oplus n}$ for multiplication by the tuple. Finite direct sums and products have the same coordinates. By the fraction equality in [def-weil-ring-localization-away], $\lambda(a)=0$ precisely when for every $i$ there is $e_i\geq1$ with $f_i^{e_i}a=0$ (increase an exponent zero to one if necessary). If $\lambda$ is injective and $\mu(a)=0$, take all $e_i=1$ to obtain $a=0$. Thus $\mu$ is injective. For these additive maps, zero kernel is equivalent to injectivity, by applying the zero-kernel assertion to a difference.

source.place: Algebra Tag 0565 (lemma-when-injective-covering), first paragraph of proof

proof.text: Conversely assume $\mu$ injective. Prove, simultaneously for all $a\in A$ and tuples $e_i\geq1$, that $f_i^{e_i}a=0$ for all $i$ implies $a=0$, by strong induction on $E=\sum_i(e_i-1)$. If $E=0$, all exponents are one, so this is $\ker\mu=0$. If $E>0$, choose $j$ with $e_j>1$ and put $b=f_ja$. The exponents $e_i$ for $i\ne j$ and $e_j-1$ for $j$ annihilate $b$, by commutativity, and have excess sum $E-1$. Induction gives $f_ja=0$. Now the original $a$ satisfies the equations with the $j$th exponent replaced by one; that excess sum is strictly smaller than $E$, so induction gives $a=0$. The fraction relation in [def-weil-ring-localization-away], as expanded in Step 1, identifies this assertion with $\ker\lambda=0$. When $n=0$, the base case asserts that the map $A\to0$ has zero kernel, exactly the injectivity hypothesis on $\mu$; both maps are the zero map and the same conclusion holds.

source.place: Algebra Tag 0565 (lemma-when-injective-covering), exponent induction in proof

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The global-section identification in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives $\mathcal O_X(X)=A$. By clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], $D(f_i)$ is affine and $\mathcal O_X(D(f_i))=A_{f_i}$ through the restriction map. By [def-weil-open-immersion], $\mathcal O_U$ is the restriction of $\mathcal O_X$. Hence a global section vanishes on $U$ if and only if it vanishes on each $D(f_i)$: one implication is restriction and the other is uniqueness in the sheaf axiom for this cover. Thus $\ker(A\to\mathcal O_U(U))=\ker\lambda$. In particular injectivity of the sheaf restriction implies injectivity of $\lambda$ by evaluation on $X$.

Assume $\lambda$ injective, hence $\mu$ injective by Step 1. Fix $g\in A$. Multiplication by the tuple $f_i/1$ is injective on $A_g$: if $f_i a/g^r=0$ for every $i$, the localization definition gives exponents $k_i$ with $g^{k_i}f_i a=0$. Take $k=\max_i k_i$ (take $k=0$ for the empty family). Then $\mu(g^ka)=0$, so $g^ka=0$, and $a/g^r=0$. Applying the already proved ring-algebra equivalence of Steps 1--2 to $A_g$ shows that $A_g\to\bigoplus_i(A_g)_{f_i/1}$ is injective.

source.place: Morphisms Tag 056C and Tag 01RE, principal-open verification; fraction argument written out

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b), $D(g)$ is affine with section ring $A_g$, and its principal open for $f_i/1$ is $D(g)\cap D(f_i)$, since the prime-ideal description in (a) tests the same element $f_i$. Its section ring is therefore $(A_g)_{f_i/1}$ via restriction. The injectivity from Step 4 says that a section on $D(g)$ vanishing on $D(g)\cap U$ is zero. The principal opens form a basis by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](i). For any open $V\subseteq X$, cover $V$ by these $D(g)\subseteq V$. A section of $\mathcal O_X(V)$ vanishing on $V\cap U$ vanishes on each basis member and hence is zero by the sheaf axiom. Therefore $\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective. This also handles the empty family: the assumed injectivity forces $A=0$, so all these section rings are zero.
